newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended Tuesday higher supported by a short-squeeze in German Bunds, after hitting a new record high in the afternoon, dealers said.
"Right now it would make sense to brace for a new profit taking wave, but I do not know if this is going to happen," a Madrid-based dealer said. "The market is doing too much".
Chart analysts put resistance at the psychological level of 108.00 and then at 108.30.
On the domestic side, the market took heart from a narrowing in the budget deficit from January to September which fell 13.2 percent compared to the prior year period.
The budget deficit had declined nine percent in the first eight months of the year.
While the ten-year benchmark bond was trading at 107.14 from 106.70 yielding 7.69 percent the 10-year spread over German Bunds was at its record low of 172 basis points.
The three-year 7.80 percent bond was at 102.78 from 102.65 yielding 6.62 percent.
Tomorrow and Thursday it is likely that the market will focus on the CPI, due on Friday. A Reuter poll showed that economists forecast CPI was 3.6 percent in September.
